subject: Renewal / expansion pricing — Acme Health volume step-ups
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-05T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: pricing follow-up + next steps (Acme Health)

Alex — thanks for taking time today. Quick recap and a couple asks so we can get a pricing proposal over to procurement: 

- Summary of priorities from the call:
  - Expand usage across customer support (chat), search/rerank, and a new summarization route for clinical notes.
  - Need predictable unit economics for budgeting; looking to move from pilot (low volume) to committed capacity over 12 months.
- Asks for us to finalize a proposal:
  1) Current baseline usage (monthly tokens) and expected step-ups over next 12 months (monthly numbers or ranges).
  2) Target budget or acceptable $/1M tokens (ballpark range helps us construct blended pricing).
  3) Any routes/models that must be included in the commitment (e.g., embeddings vs. gen vs. rerank).

We’ll draft a stepped pricing schedule and a blended estimate that covers mixed route usage (we typically do per-1M token bands with optional add-on model premiums). I’ve looped in Dev for any technical clarifications.

If you can share the numbers by EOD tomorrow we’ll push a formal proposal and estimated DocuSign to procurement.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>

Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-03-05T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: pricing follow-up + next steps (Acme Health)

Marissa — thanks for the recap. Apologies for the late reply; pulled numbers from our usage team. High-level: 

- Current baseline: ~12M tokens/month (pilot: chat + light summarization).
- Expected step-ups: we expect a staged ramp — 25M/mo by Q3, 40M/mo by end of year, and steady-state goal ~60M/mo within 12 months if the expansion goes well.
- Routes to include in commitment: chat (gen), summarization (longer context), and search-rerank (rerank/embeddings mix). Gen usage is ~65% of tokens today, rerank/embeddings ~25%, summarization ~10% (these percentages may shift).
- Budget target: we'd like to aim for ~$500–$800 per 1M tokens (ballpark). Our procurement/finance prefers to see blended per-1M estimates across routes rather than separate line items.
- Timeline: procurement aims to finish contracting in 2–3 weeks once we have final commercial terms and the DocuSign.

Happy to hop on another quick call if helpful.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Product Integrations, Acme Health
alex.johnson@acmehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-03-06T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: stepped pricing + blended estimate (draft) — Acme Health

Alex — thanks for the numbers. Attached is a draft pricing sketch and a short blended example for the 40M/mo scenario. High-level proposal (draft, subject to legal/procurement redlines):

- Stepped list price per 1M tokens (generation-heavy workload):
  - 0–10M: $1,000 / 1M tokens
  - 10–25M: $900 / 1M tokens
  - 25–50M: $700 / 1M tokens
  - 50M+: $500 / 1M tokens
- Model premiums / route notes (applied as %):
  - Rerank/embeddings: +10% on per-1M for high-cost retrieval models (unless run on smaller embedding models)
  - Summarization (long context): +15% for longer-context model variants
- Blended example for 40M/mo (using your mix: gen 65% / rerank 25% / summarization 10%):
  - Effective blended rate ≈ $650 / 1M tokens (illustrative).

Next steps we recommend:
1) Internal technical sync (30–45m) with Dev to confirm prompt mix, tail latencies, and any memory/throughput requirements that affect pricing (e.g., very long contexts).
2) We finalize a 12-month committed capacity schedule (monthly step-ups) and produce a procurement-ready quote + DocuSign.
3) Optionally add a dedicated reserved pool for peak traffic — we can include a reserved-capacity credit to offset unit price.

Attaching: redwood-pricing-proposal-v3.pdf (formal draft with band math), usage-projections-2026.xlsx (filled with illustrative month-by-month ramp).

If this looks directionally OK I’ll send the procurement-ready quote and a DocuSign link for review.

Thanks —
Marissa

Attachments: redwood-pricing-proposal-v3.pdf, usage-projections-2026.xlsx

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-03-07T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Proposal: stepped pricing + blended estimate (draft) — Acme Health

Alex / Marissa — quick tech notes to align expectations before procurement: 

- Model choice materially affects per-token cost (larger models + longer contexts -> higher GPU utilization). If your rerank route can use a smaller embedding model for most traffic we can keep those tokens at the lower band.
- For summarization with long context (>8k tokens) we recommend a long-context model variant; that’s where the +15% premium above applies.
- To produce a final blended estimate we need a short sample prompt mix (typical prompt + avg response length) per route. Can you drop a small sample in the shared sheet?
- Ops note: if you want predictable latency for peak windows we can include a Dedicated reserved capacity quote — that changes the economics (we’ll show a reserved credit in the final DocuSign).

If it helps, we can run a 2-week canary on Dedicated to validate latency/cost before a full commit.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
